exclusions.delivery: the close that follows: a delivered agent is then closed through the scripted fakes; the replay compares only whether the table reads the agent as delivered (`closed`) or not (`undelivered`)
exclusions.dispatch: the daemon's hidden set: Node hides a session in its own hidden set (runtime/shared/session-hidden.mjs), which the recorder seeds from the world's `hidden` and which is not one of the logged collaborators; the core hides by the session header's archivedAt, and a replay seeds its fake of that from the same list. Which sessions a cleanup hid is compared through the count in the answer

keptWhole: dispatch: per scenario its arguments, context and world, the effect calls in order and the rendered answer; delivery: per scenario its steps and the state releaseIdle answered

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

syntheticInputs: dispatch: the registry, views and session manager are the scripted fakes of native/core/fixtures/agent/record-agent-tool.mjs; sessionGone, isSessionTurnInFlight and listSessions answer from the world and log nothing; every job of a world is running
delivery: the jobs are put on the real table and ended by the table's own calls; no notifier is attached, so a completion goes out to nobody
